absent: Encodings and full effects of trampoline generation, mapping helpers and hardening selection macros.
Complete layout of thread processor context and task floating point structures beyond fields referenced here.
Full delegated exception event record layout, priority values and exit mode encodings.
Tables of supported vector lengths, architectural maximum and default length values.
Synchronisation for default length updates and CPU mask updates beyond the interrupt discipline shown.
Internals of scheduler tail, user mode exit preparation, pointer authentication install and shadow stack helpers.

findings.text: Trampoline vector store supplies kernel page table isolation entry points with selectable branch history hardening variants when that mitigation is configured, always retaining a fallback with no hardening.
Trampoline exit path unmaps kernel address space, restores the saved frame pointer from the fault address register, then returns from exception followed by a speculation barrier.
Hardened exception vectors for privileged execution provide alternative branch predictor hardening implementations chosen at build time when branch history mitigation is enabled.

Context switch exchanges callee preserved registers, stack pointer and link register between previous and next thread storage, advertises the next task through the EL0 stack register, refreshes pointer authentication keys and shadow stack state, and restores the prior interrupt mask before returning.

Fork return completes scheduler tail handling then separates kernel threads, which call their start routine with its argument, from other tasks, which prepare for user mode exit and resume in user space.

Delegated exception trampoline entry tests whether the current translation base indicates user mappings and maps the kernel only in that case, recording the decision in the event record before jumping to the shared handler; the paired exit reads the record and unmaps only when entry had mapped.

Shared delegated exception handler preserves the interrupted register file into the event area, records the event as the active normal or critical event according to priority, moves to the corresponding per CPU stack and shadow stack, and reloads the EL0 stack base from the per CPU entry task because interrupted stack state cannot be trusted.

After the high level handler returns, assembly selects plain completion or completion with resume by comparing the result with the failure threshold, clears the active event marker for the observed priority, and either exits directly or branches to the exit trampoline depending on whether kernel unmapping at EL0 is configured; the abort variant always requests completion with resume to a local continuation.
Exception flag FPEXC_IOF occupies bit zero, FPEXC_DZF bit one, FPEXC_OFF bit two, FPEXC_UFF bit three, FPEXC_IXF bit four, and FPEXC_IDF bit seven.

Floating point tracking keeps a per CPU record of the last resident state, a per vector type table with type tag, name and length bounds where the SVE entry starts at its minimum, and a per type configuration holding the default length applied to tasks.
Inherit flag helper returns TIF_SVE_VL_INHERIT for the SVE type and TIF_SME_VL_INHERIT for the SME type, warning and returning zero for any other type.

Default length controls expose ABI entries sve_default_vector_length and sme_default_vector_length that read the current default and on write treat minus one as maximum request, reject invalid values, round to a supported length and store it; setup registers each entry under abi only when its extension is present and reports failure if registration fails.
Alternate initialisers for builds without the corresponding extension do nothing and report success.

Synchronisation from scalable state copies the low portion of each scalable register into the matching FPSIMD register for the task current length, doing nothing when neither SVE nor SME is present; a companion helper clears all FPSIMD vector registers.

Leaving streaming mode does nothing when streaming is already inactive, otherwise it clears vector state, installs default status, clears the floating point mode register when available, clears streaming mode bits and demotes the saved state type to FPSIMD.

Per CPU enablement prepares SVE, SME, SME2 full A64 and floating point mode features by setting control registers to known defaults, granting EL1 and EL0 access where required, enforcing ordering so dependent features enable after SME, and restoring SME defaults on suspend exit.

Live length changes allocate replacement state before releasing the old to survive allocation failure without mutation, flush hardware state for current or other tasks, preserve streaming mode and FPSIMD content while zeroing extended portions, and for SME also clear the ZA mode bit and replace SME storage.

Length set validates flags and value, clamps oversized requests to the architectural maximum, rounds to a supported length, updates live state immediately unless deferred to exec, records on exec value and inherit choice, while status reports either live or on exec length with inherit indication.

Current length interfaces for SVE and SME split the argument into length and flags, reject requests on systems lacking the extension or for compat tasks, delegate mutation to the shared setter and report resulting status on set or current status on get.

Floating point paths assume interrupt protection with thread switch requiring disabled interrupts and state binding requiring disabled interrupts or soft interrupt context, bracket save and flush work with CPU context acquire and release, and defer freeing of replaced state until after leaving atomic context.

Thread switch saves outgoing user or kernel floating state, then for incoming kernel threads flushes CPU state and loads kernel state with elision when the same state already resides on the same CPU, otherwise marks the incoming user state foreign when task or CPU differs.

Exec reset zeroes FPSIMD state, drops scalable and matrix storage, reestablishes each length from on exec value or system default with validation and support rounding, clears extension flags and control state and resets type to FPSIMD; task release frees remaining scalable and matrix storage with a no-op variant when the matrix extension is absent.

Invalid lengths, unknown flags and unknown vector types are rejected or warned about rather than applied, allocation failure during length change preserves prior state and reports out of memory, and failed control registration reports invalid argument.
Conversion arm64_le128_to_cpu is defined as identical to arm64_cpu_to_le128.

Matrix extension synchronisation tracks participating and active CPUs in dedicated masks, while its inter processor handler intentionally does nothing because exception entry with enhanced synchronisation guarantees completion.

Current state helpers save user state with CPU protection, either flushing task association afterwards, preserving without flushing, or installing a caller supplied FPSIMD image and re exporting to scalable representation when active, each doing nothing when FPSIMD is absent.

Delegated exception handling cannot trust the interrupted stack pointer or EL0 base because entry may have used the stack as scratch or interrupted user, guest or transitional code, so it switches to dedicated stacks and reloads the base; abort completion destroys volatile registers and processor state before continuing.
